issues.message: Exponential backtracking (proven). Severity: CRITICAL, confidence: HIGH.
issues.hint: Attack: "" . "!" x n . "<" Replayed on PCRE2 10.49: preg_match fails from length 24 (backtrack_limit 100000, JIT off). The risky part is: [^<]* Hotspot offsets: 9-14 Quantifier repeats a subpattern that can match empty. This creates ambiguous backtracking paths and can be catastrophic. Nested unbounded quantifiers detected. This allows exponential backtracking. Consider using atomic groups (?>...) or possessive quantifiers (*+, ++). Suggested (verify behavior): Ensure the repeated subpattern consumes at least one character, or wrap it in (?>...) / use possessive quantifiers. Suggested (verify behavior): Replace inner quantifiers with possessive variants or wrap them in (?>...). Suggested (verify behavior): replace nested quantifiers like (a+)+ with atomic groups (?>a+) or possessive quantifiers a++. Suggested (verify behavior): replace * with *+ in groups to prevent backtracking or wrap in (?>...). Test with adversarial inputs like repeated strings followed by a non-matching character.

findings.pattern:
{
				(?:\n|\A)
				# 1: Opening marker
				(
					~{3,} # Marker: three tilde or more.
				)
				[ ]* \n # Whitespace and newline following marker.

				# 2: Content
				(
					(?>
						(?!\1 [ ]* \n)	# Not a closing marker.
						.*\n+
					)+
				)

				# Closing marker.
				\1 [ ]* \n
			}xm

{
				(?:\n|\A)
				# 1: Opening marker
				(
					~{3,} # Marker: three tilde or more.
				)
				[ ]* \n # Whitespace and newline following marker.

				# 2: Content
				(
					(?>
						(?!\1 [ ]* \n)	# Not a closing marker.
						.*\n+
					)+
				)

				# Closing marker.
				\1 [ ]* \n
			}x

		   [\x09\x0A\x0D\x20-\x7E]            # ASCII

		 | \xE0[\xA0-\xBF][\x80-\xBF]         # excluding overlongs
		 | [\xE1-\xEC\xEE\xEF][\x80-\xBF]{2}  # straight 3-byte
		 | \xED[\x80-\x9F][\x80-\xBF]         # excluding surrogates
		 | \xF0[\x90-\xBF][\x80-\xBF]{2}      # planes 1-3
		 | [\xF1-\xF3][\x80-\xBF]{3}          # planes 4-15
		 | \xF4[\x80-\x8F][\x80-\xBF]{2}      # plane 16
		)*$%xs
